NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions and residual connections provide a structural basis for tracing historical context, but theoretical receptive field does not establish which interactions affect rankings. Its original paper motivates dilation for long-range dependencies; activation interventions could measure their actual use. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163). The strongest directly relevant methodological results found were from 2024: patching conclusions depend on corruption choice, measurement metric, and intervention direction. Clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption test different properties; redundancy can obscure single-block effects. [Heimersheim & Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255).

Proposed NextItNet adaptation: construct paired histories perturbing older versus recent nonpadding items, matching replacement count, positions and item-frequency ranges. Preserve sequence length, left-padding mask and final-nonpadding readout. Patch individual residual-branch outputs at selected positions, recompute downstream layers, and measure fixed-candidate score margins alongside rank changes. Whole residual-stream patches can restore information carried through skip connections, so branch-specific or path interventions are needed to distinguish transmission routes. Attribution patching offers an inexpensive screening approximation; confirm selected sites with actual interventions. [Syed et al., 2024](https://aclanthology.org/2024.blackboxnlp-1.25/).

Controls should include identity patches, matched random sites, multiple corruption samples, both patch directions and paired-block interventions to expose interactions. Report raw effects when normalized recovery has a near-zero denominator. Parameter-randomization checks test whether attribution depends on learned weights, although their interpretation also requires care. [Adebayo et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03292), [Fresh Look, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.02383). These experiments support claims about model pathways under specified interventions; they do not establish user intent.
